key_insight: PARA-PV improves photovoltaic forecasting by combining physics-aware retrieval of similar historical patterns with a frozen foundation-model prior and distribution-shift correction tailored to PV regimes.
engineering_relevance: The approach can make solar power forecasts more reliable for grid dispatch by better handling weather changes, day-night transitions, and critical ramping or peak events.
method: Retrieve historical patches and analog trajectories matched by temporal shape, power level, operating state, and intra-day period.
Blend the retrieved forecast with a frozen Chronos prior using a lightweight residual adapter.
Apply physics-aware distribution-shift correction and a regime-weighted loss for peak, ramping, night-time, and regular samples.
evidence_signal: The abstract indicates the method is evaluated for PV power forecasting across physically distinct regimes, but it does not report specific metrics or dataset size.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of retrieval matches and on carefully designed gating so the correction module does not distort physically grounded forecasts.
paper_title: PARA-PV: Physics-Aware Retrieval-Augmented PV Prediction Based on Frozen Foundation Model and Distribution Shift Correction
